newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice steady to lower this week, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice steady to lower this week, slow trade.

text.p: The Thai rice market remained quiet as exporters slowed down buying and awaited an easing of prices, trade sources said on Thursday.
While benchmark 100 percent white B rice prices were steady to lower, prices of the premium grade fragrant rice rose sharply.
The benchmark 100 percent white B was quoted at around US$335-$340 per tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $338-$340 last week.

Fragrant rice was quoted at around $600 per tonne FOB Bagnkok compared with $585 last week and an average of $528 in August as supplies were tight amid depleting stocks due to robust demand in recent months.
Traders said exporters slowed down buying of 100 percent white B grade in a bid to force prices down. Demand also eased as foreign buyers were sidelined by high prices.
"The prices of Thai rice are too high compared with those of Vietnam and India. It doesn't give much incentive to buy at the moment," said one trader.
But the prices barely dropped because only small amount of supply entered the market as millers slowed down activity to support prices.
Thailand had exported 74,314 tonnes of rice in the week ended September 22, compared with 67,590 tonnes a week earlier.
At the Bangkok port, vessels were loading 35,200 tonnes of rice for shipment to Asian and African destinations.
